note: Majority: the Children Act (Cap. 59), as published by the Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development (mglsd.go.ug/laws), section 2: a child is a person below the age of eighteen years. The form holds 18 as the age of majority on that definition (my reading; the Contracts Act 2010's own capacity rule was not read). Work: the Employment Act 2006 (Act 6 of 2006), the ministry's scanned copy, read by eye on 2026-10-31 (it has no text layer): s. 32(1) a child under twelve shall not be employed in any business, undertaking or workplace; s. 32(2) a child under fourteen shall not be employed except for light work under the supervision of an adult over eighteen which does not affect the child's education; s. 32(4)-(5) no injurious or hazardous work and no work between 7 p.m. and 7 a.m. So general employment from 14, light work from 12, which the form doesn't hold. Performers: the Act makes no exception for performing; a performer under 14 is held to the same rule (light work from 12 only), so the form holds barred (my reading of the Act's silence). The Children (Amendment) Act 2016 was saved from the same ministry page but is a scanned 55-page document and was not read for any change to these ages; the Stage Plays and Public Entertainments Act (Cap. 49) on the same page was not read. Service: null. Uganda has no conscription to my knowledge, but no source saying so was read: the UPDF's site (updf.go.ug) answered with a captcha and wasn't pursued, State House's constitution page was missing (404) and Parliament's did not answer.

sources.title: The Children Act, Cap. 59 (Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development)
sources.said: A child is a person below the age of eighteen years.

sources.title: The Employment Act, 2006 (Act 6), scanned copy, Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development
sources.said: 32. Employment of Children (1) A child under the age of twelve years shall not be employed in any business, undertaking or work place. (2) A child under the age of fourteen years shall not be employed in any business, undertaking or workplace, except for light work carried out under supervision of an adult aged over eighteen years, and which does not affect the child’s education.
